title: fix: double hook execution
body:
Continuing the discussion about this issue:
- https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/4959
- Previous tentative: https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/4963 (rollback https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/5008)

To replicate the issue:

1. follow these instructions: https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/4959#issuecomment-2631937444
2. run `npx autocannon -m PUT -c 1 -d 1 http://localhost:3000/ -b '{ "test": "me" }' -H "Content-Type: application/json"` (it does not happen always, but 2/3 or run fails for me)

From my experiment, when we resolve the thenable:

https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/30b81299c5b8b2dca9db20558a440c5c2b424660/lib/reply.js#L473

The output of this line:  
 `console.log('fulfilled: ', this.raw.writableEnded, this.raw.destroyed, this.raw.aborted, err)` is:
- working: `fulfilled:  true true undefined undefined`
- crash: `fulfilled:  false true undefined Error [ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE]: Premature close`

By reading the comments, I see the `ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE` error is skipped because it is set by [`eos`](https://nodejs.org/api/stream.html#writabledestroyerror)

https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/30b81299c5b8b2dca9db20558a440c5c2b424660/lib/reply.js#L464-L465

Should we?

issues.title: onSend hook can be called twice
comments: The bug is due to the unreliability of `aborted`. It should be replaced with `destroyed`.
I'm finding a bit hard to write a unit test for this, as I cannot replicate the exact condition that leads to this double execution.

> The bug is due to the unreliability of aborted. It should be replaced with destroyed.

Regarding the `.aborted` property, I don't think it is unreliable.
Changing from `.aborted` to `.destroyed` only fixed the outcomes, but the underlying issue of forked thenable chain is not fixed.
And as I remembered correctly, it is once changed to `.destoryed` and it breaks too many.

> Then call from autocannon and abort the request.

The bug is interesting since when you increase the amount of request, it cannot be reproduced anymore.
Yes, it is reproduced only when the request number is 5 and using `autocannon`.

What puzzles me on this bug is how [this](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/b4b4dc7568e7b0bcff7f71a63f8c9630e4cab232/lib/wrapThenable.js#L21C35-L21C129) could evaluate to true, _after_ a `reply.send()` was called already one time.

> What puzzles me on [this](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/b4b4dc7568e7b0bcff7f71a63f8c9630e4cab232/lib/wrapThenable.js#L21C35-L21C129) bug is how this could evaluate to true, after a reply.send() was called already one time.

The whole issue is when the request is terminated in the middle, which is the case where `autocannon` is not specified `amount`.

It leads to the problem of `reply.then` and `eos` called earlier than it should. Yes, we forked the thenable chain ourselves.

https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/b4b4dc7568e7b0bcff7f71a63f8c9630e4cab232/lib/reply.js#L464-L476

> It leads to the problem of reply.then and eos called earlier than it should. Yes, we forked the thenable chain ourselves.

Indeed we did and for good reason: supporting `reply.send()`.

In theory wrapThenable handles this case by checking the `aborted` property, but for some unfortunate reason that is not set in this case. I've been trying to reproduce this for a few hours with nothing to show.

> I've been trying to reproduce this for a few hours with nothing to show.

The problem only occur when a network connection lost, which means it is hard to do so using `node.js` only.
It is reproducible using the `autocannon` command line only because it has a `timer` to forcefully shutdown the whole process and leaving the unprocessed request there.

https://github.com/mcollina/autocannon/blob/ec3c7555c6ba26fe6a82783520b39138f9918374/lib/run.js#L88-L92

We might want an additional guard by `&& !reply.raw.socket?.destroyed` to ensure the `reply.send` inside thenable only called when the socket still available and writable.
1. Properly cleanup request would result in `socket === undefined`
2. Destroyed socket would result in `socket.destroyed === true`
Unfortunately this introduced a bad regression (see https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/5008), so we would need to find a different fix for this.
I don't experience this bug, so while it's pretty bad, I don't have much time to research a different fix.

I've been digging into this lately, and I've seen a similar pattern when you error within your `onSend` hook.
Fastify handles the error, but re-calls the same hook once more, although the `onSend` already was called.

Introducing a small flag that states the hooks already ran should _solve the issue_ (similar to what we did for handling errors as part of the `reply.send` process).

This fix can most likely have the side effect of blocking duplicated hooks from running.

Unless the `onSend` hook is called twice even when handling errors thrown from the same hook was made with this intention by design.
Note that the double call is ok in the latter case. Specifically because is onSend that fails.

evidence.body:
This needs sth like

```suggestion
        reply.request.socket != null &&
        !reply.request.socket.destroyed
```
